clue.text: One not paying attention follows investor's vehicle

indicators.note: something that follows comes after, so the inattentive one is placed second

parts.note: a bull is an investor who expects prices to rise; the 's links it to the vehicle
someone dozing off is not paying attention

explanation.surface: An absent-minded passenger trails along behind a wealthy investor's car.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stock market a bull bets on rising prices; read 'investor’s vehicle' as BULL'S followed by a sleepy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldozer is a heavy tracked machine for clearing ground, a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Strange ladies swaddle in newborn, this could be a lifesaver

indicators.note: swaddling wraps a baby, so the ladies are wrapped around the strange word
the wrapped bundle goes inside the remade word
new means made fresh, so the following word is remade in another order

parts.note: first letter of the second half of this word, rearranged
the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo; it is split around the next piece
strange means odd
the rest of the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Strange women bundle up a baby; perhaps this saves a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newborn' must be split in two: 'new' is the instruction and the four letters after it are the material. Two wrappings nest, like a baby swaddled and then held.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives blood for transfusions can save patients' lives, hence a lifesaver.

clue.text: Look around this country and love the record

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps about the others

parts.note: taken as written, opened up to hold the rest
Great Britain, this country from the British setter's viewpoint
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to tour the nation and cherish its history.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British paper 'this country' is Great Britain, and love is zero, from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A logbook is an official written record, as of a ship's voyage or a car's details.

clue.text: Study why said alibi mostly inconsistent and keep in custody

indicators.note: mostly means all except the last letter

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study

indicators.note: something inconsistent does not hold to one form, so the letters change order
said means spoken, so the word before is heard rather than read

parts.note: the letter that is pronounced like this word
the word less its final letter

explanation.surface: A detective asks why a suspect's story keeps changing, and decides to hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: When a court refuses release on surety pending trial, the accused stays locked up.

clue.text: He or she regularly groom for nothing

parts.note: ze is a gender-neutral pronoun used in place of he or she

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Either partner tidies themselves up at set intervals without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He or she' is not two words to pick from: it defines a modern neutral pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number meaning none at all, nought.

clue.text: Moved at speed, firing and looting

parts.note: to run is to move fast; past tense
firing an employee is sacking them

explanation.surface: A rampaging gang rushes about, shooting and plundering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' suggests guns, but it means dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransacking means searching through a place and stealing from it, i.e. plundering.

clue.text: Heath Robinson's beat

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer belongs to, and sits inside, the name before it

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two names

explanation.surface: A remark about the rhythm or patrol of the cartoonist Heath Robinson.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist known for absurdly complicated machines; the answer straddles his two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a rhythmic pulse, as a heart's beat or a drum's pounding.

clue.text: Bosses get the best hands

parts.note: the top is the best
a hand is a bunch of bananas, so hands are bananas

explanation.surface: Managers are dealt the strongest cards in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggests card games, but a cluster of bananas on the stalk is called a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A top banana is informal slang for the most important person in a group, a leader.

clue.text: They help players or back a side when playing

parts.note: read in the opposite direction

indicators.note: back means going backwards, the short word read right to left
playing about with letters jumbles their order

parts.note: these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Teammates either help each other or support their side during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' sounds like sport, but here it means musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadies are the crew who set up gear and assist touring bands, helping the musicians.

clue.text: Hurt actor (one in a minor role)

parts.note: bit, the past of bite, as in hurt with teeth
an actor plays parts

explanation.surface: An injured performer is mentioned, with a bracketed aside about the part.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small part in a play or film, and the performer who takes one is so called.

clue.text: This operation could make you groan

definitions.text: This operation could make you groan

parts.words: This operation could make you groan
parts.note: surface reading: a painful surgical procedure that leaves the patient moaning
setter's reading: rearrange the letters of a musical instrument's name and you get this word

explanation.walkthrough: Transplant the letters of ORGAN around and they spell GROAN, so the operation literally makes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving a kidney or heart from donor to patient is a major surgical operation of this name.

clue.text: Kind of gorgeous exit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the phrase that intensifies 'gorgeous' to mean stunningly attractive
second meaning: to exit life suddenly, to die on the spot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'exit' is a euphemism for dying rather than leaving a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning looks are called drop-dead gorgeous, and to collapse and die abruptly is to drop dead.

clue.text: Grandfather initially isn't at all moved

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word that follows is kept, the rest is dropped

parts.note: the second half of this word, father, is pa; the first half is the definition

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are shifted out of their order

parts.note: its first letter only
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man remains entirely unaffected, unmoved by events.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandfather must be split: 'Grand' is the definition and 'father' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial means like a palace, so splendid and imposing, which is what grand describes.

clue.text: Culture retrospective on wobbly bums is a problem for viewers

parts.note: culture as the arts, read backwards

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the word is read backwards
wobbly means unsteady, so these letters lose their places

parts.note: these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An art exhibition of jiggling buttocks troubles the gallery-goers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' looks like an exhibition but turns the arts word round; viewers are eyes, not visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabismus is a squint, a misalignment of the eyes, so it troubles a person's sight.

clue.text: Philistine's request? Of course, you're welcome

parts.note: Philistine is the setter, who refers to himself as me
a plea is an appeal or request
sure as in certainly

explanation.surface: The setter asks for something and is gracious in reply to thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Philistine is the name of this puzzle's setter, so his possessive is 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies to someone who has just thanked you.

clue.text: Chatter yet to be arranged between oxen

indicators.note: something set between two things sits inside them

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox; the plural supplies one either side

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters into a new order

parts.note: these three letters rearranged
the second of the pair

explanation.surface: An instruction to schedule some small talk among the cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxen' is plural, so it supplies two yaks, one either side of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakety-yak is informal for idle, incessant talk, the same as chatter.

clue.text: I'm your child and I find this chat tedious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: you gave birth to me, bore being the past of bear
second meaning: a blunt complaint that the talker is dull

explanation.walkthrough: The same three words read as a mother's role in childbirth and as a rude put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Your mother bore you, and a dull talker bores the listener, so the phrase covers both.

clue.text: Like state analysis

parts.note: as in 'like' meaning in the manner of
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like an analysis of a nation or its condition.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test of a metal or substance to determine its composition, a chemical analysis.

clue.text: Hesitation having underwear in this shade

parts.note: the sound of someone hesitating
an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: Someone dithers while wearing lingerie in a darkened spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, as during an eclipse, so a deep shade.

clue.text: Surprise from Glasgow in cheese and bread

indicators.note: in places the exclamation inside the cheese

parts.note: a soft French cheese, opened up
och is a Scottish exclamation of surprise or dismay

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian is startled by a ploughman's lunch of cheese and bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a light, sweet French bread enriched with eggs and butter.

clue.text: City's ancestral manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are movements and repositionings, so these letters are shifted about

parts.note: all nine letters used

explanation.surface: A city's inherited military exercises, passed down through generations.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a historic English city in Lancashire, the county town.

clue.text: This pet can be truly awful

indicators.note: can be implies these letters could become something else when reordered

parts.note: all seven letters used

explanation.surface: An exasperated owner complains that their animal is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something the pits is slang for saying it is the worst, utterly dreadful.

clue.text: Novel and one drink allowed in exam

indicators.note: being allowed in means being admitted inside, so these go within the test

parts.note: a spoken examination
the Roman numeral for one
a spirit

explanation.surface: An unusual rule permitting a single drink during an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces join, then sit inside the spoken test, which opens round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means new and fresh, not copied, which is what original describes.

clue.text: See 10
See 1
Olympic rider's best run taking only second place

indicators.note: only the second letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: second letter
second letter
second letter
second letter

explanation.surface: An equestrian's top round earns only silver at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second place' looks like a podium finish; 'place' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in the phrase 'in lieu of', instead of.

clue.text: See 3
Church ban for telegram?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: formal exclusion from the sacraments of the church
second meaning, read whimsically: a former kind of message, now obsolete

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the joke: a telegram is an ex-communication, a means of communicating that is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from the church's rites is the formal ecclesiastical punishment of this name.

clue.text: Pitchers were out first on stadium

indicators.note: out suggests thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged
placed on means set after, the next piece added at the end

parts.note: these four letters rearranged

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the word that follows

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Baseball pitchers were dismissed early at the ballpark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitchers' suggests baseball players, but it means jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug with a wide spout, so ewers are pitchers for water.

clue.text: Most of all, queries must be directed to reach the goal

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter
being directed means being steered into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word less its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly every question should be routed through proper channels to get to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' here is a football score that levels the match, not an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An equaliser is the score that brings a team level, typically in football.
